Homage to Martyrs of the Quit India Movement 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, on the 9th August, 2003 feel the 
sixty-first anniversary of the historic day when the Quit India Movement 
was launched by the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi, in 1942. 
There was an overwhelming response to the clarion call of Gandhiji. 
Men, women, and even children came out in large numbers to participate 
in the movement with total dedication and commitment. This 
spontaneous upsurge of nationalistic sentiments culminated later, after 
five years, in our attaining Independence. 
We pay our respectful tributes to the martyrs who sacrificed their 
lives and to those who had undergone untold sufferings for the cause 
of our freedom. 
I would request Members to rise in  their places and observe silence 
as a mark of respect to the memory of the martyrs of our freedom 
struggle. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
Crash of ONGC Helicopter 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon Members, as you are aware, on Monday, the 
11 th August, 2003. a chartered helicopter, Mi-172, which was ferrying 29 
persons, 25 ONGC employees and four crew members, crashed into the 
Arabian Sea around 77 kilometres off the Mumbai coast. The crash 
occurred two minutes after the helicopter took off from the oil rig, Sagar 
Kiran, at Bombay High.The search is still on for those who are missing. 
I am sure that the whole House will joint me to pray for the missing 
persons and mourn the death of those  who were killed in this worst 

RAJYA SABHA [13 August, 2003] 
helicopter disaster. We also extend our heartfelt condolences to the affected 
families. 
I now request Members to rise in their places and observe silence to 
 mourn the death of those who were killed in the accident. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute)

Savings under SJGSY 
†*326. SHRIMATI KUM KUM RAI:  Will the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether women are being encouraged to cultivate habit of savings 
under Swarn Jyanti Gram Swarojzar Yojana; 
(b) if so, whether Government are also contributing any amount as 
incentive to the amount of savings done under this scheme; and 
(c) if so, the district-wise details in respect of Bihar during the financial 
year 2001 -2002? 
THE MINISTER OF RURAL DE VELOPMENT (SHRI KASHIRAM 
RANA): (a) to (c) Under Swarn Jayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY), 
Self-Help Groups (SHGs) of rural poor, including those of women, are 
encouraged to cultivated the habit of saving through thrift & credit 
activities.The Self-Help Groups (SHGs),  which are in existence for about 
six months and have demonstrated the potential of a viable group are 
provided with Revolving Fund Assistance (RFA) from District Rural 
Development Agency (DRDA) and Banks as a cash credit facility. The 
DRDAs release subsidy which is equal to the group corpus with a 
minimum of Rs. 5,000/- and a maximum of Rs. 10,000/-. The Banks can 
sanction credit which could go up to four times of the group corpus. The

Details of Nirmal Gram Puraskar Scheme 
The sanitation coverage in the rural areas of the country has 
been only 20% at the beginning of the 10th Plan. Government of 
India have been promoting the sanitation coverage on a campaign 
mode to ensure better health and quality of life for people in the rural 
areas. Government of India have approved an incentive scheme for 
fully sanitized and open defecation free Gram Panchayats, Blocks 
and Districts.

The Puraskar scheme have the following ingredients: 
(i) Eligibility:

sanitation coverage in terms of (a) 100% sanitation coverage of 
individual house holds, (b) 100% school sanitation coverage 
(c) free from open defecation and (d) clean environment 
maintenance. 
* Individuals and organizations, who have been the driving force 
for effecting full sanitation coverage in the respective geographical 
area.

(SHRI HARIN PATHAK): (a) No, Sir. There has been a progressive decline 
in the crime rate of Delhi during the past few years.

in their Study Report into the manpower and modernization needs of Delhi 
Police made wide ranging recommendations covering practically all the 
aspects of police functioning including norms for setting up of new Police 
Stations; crime investigation; traffic management; upgradation of training 
facilities; augmentation of security units; and modernization of arms and 
equipment. The Government have accepted most of the recommendations 
in principle and it has been decided to implement these in a phased manner

Proposed amendment in marriage laws 
2446. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government propose to amend the marriage laws to protect 
women from litigation-related harassment, if so, the details of the enabling 
provisions; and 
60 

[13 August, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
(b) whether Government also propose to bring in some kind of legislation 
to legalize "live-in-arrangement" practice, which is gaining ground? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI I.D. SWAMI): (a) Government introduced on 9th May, 2003 The 
Marriage Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2003' in Rajya Sabha in order to 
identify the areas of harassment, etc.  to women. The Bill proposes to 
amend the Special Marriage Act, 19 54 and Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, 
so that a wife can also file petition in the district court within whose 
local limits of jurisdiction she may be residing. The Bill also proposes 
to amend provisions of the said Acts to provide that the parties to a 
matrimonial suit may prefer an appeal within a period of 90 days instead

recommended that section 494 of Indian Penal Code may be amended 
to the effect that if a man and wo man were living together as husband 
and wife for a reasonably long period, the man shall be deemed to have 
married the woman according to the customary rites of either party.

and

(SHRI I.D. SWAMl): (a) Section 3(1) of the Commissions of inquiry Act, 
80 

[13 August, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
1952 provides that the appropriate Government may, if it is of opinion 
that it is necessary so to do, and shall, if a resolution in this behalf is 
passed by each House of Parliame nt or, as the case may be, the 
Legislature of the State, by notificati on in the Official Gazette, appoint a 
Commission of Inquiry for the purpose of making an inquiry into any 
definite matter of public importance and performing such functions and 
within such time as may be specified in the notification, and the 
Commission so appointed shall make the inquiry and perform the 
functions accordingly. 
Section 3(4) of the Act provides that the appropriate Government 
shall cause to be laid before each House of Parliament or, as the case 
may be, the Legislature of the State, the report, if any, of the Commission 
on the inquiry made by the Commission under sub-section (1) together 
with a memorandum of the action taken thereon, within a period of six 
months of the submission of the report by the Commission to the 
appropriate Government. 
Since sufficient provisions already exist in the Act regarding mode of 
appointment of Inquiry Commission, its terms of reference, make its 
findings and recommendations public and inspire confidence in its 
indepenence, there is no proposal to amend the Commissions of Inquiry 
Act, 1952.

2498. SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI: 
                 DR.T. SUBBARAMI REDDY: 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have approved an additional Rs. 700 Crore 
for three schemes for improving supply of drinking water in rural India; 
(b) if so, what are the three schemes for which this amount has been 
sanctioned; 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
139 

RAJYA SABHA [13 August, 2003] 
(c) whetherr the amount sanctioned is sufficient for completing those 
projects; 
(d) whether according to the study conducted by Government, the 
main areas of concern in the rural water supply sector was coverage of 
habitations including schools in the rural areas and ensuring sustainability 
of systems and sourrces; and 
(e) if so, what are the steps suggested by them in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI ANNASAHEB M.K. PATIL): (a) to (c) Yes Sir, 
Rs. 700 Crore have been approved for three programmes viz. 
(i) Installation of 1 -lakh-hand pumps, (ii) revival of 1 -lakh traditional sources 
of water and (iii) providing drinking water facility in 1-lakh rural primary 
schools. The total cost for implementation of these programme is Rs. 
800 Crores. Rs. 80 Crores (10%) will be the community participation and 
Rs. 20 crores will be utilised from the existing provisions. 
(d) and (e) Coverage of habitations and ensuring sustainability of systems 
and sources are the main areas of concern in the Rural Water Supply 
Sector. Experience has shown that supply driven non-participatory approach 
has led to the failure of some water supply systems and sources. It was 
felt that participatory demand driven approach will ensure sustainbility. With 
this aim reforms were initiated in 1999 in 67 sector Reform Pilot Project. 
The reform initiatives have now been scaled up to cover the entire country 
by launching the swajaldhara programme on 25th December, 2002.

Study Conducted by the Textile Committee 
2539. SHRIMATI N.R DURGA : Will the Minister of TEXTILES be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that accord ing to a study conducted by the 
Textile Committee to.assess the impact of reforms on the functioning of 
the Committee said that reforms su cceeded in changing the Committee 
from abominable regulations to growth-led facilitation; and 
(b) what are the other major outcome of study conducted by the 
Textile Committee? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES 
(SHRI BASAN GOUDA R. PATIL): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir.The major outcome 
of the study conducted by the Textiles Committee are as under:— 
1. The Textiles Committee, which used to be primarily an 
Inspection Agency till early 1990s, has oriented itself to 
become a facilitator in assisting the textile industry, in quality 
improvement in the wake of withdrawal of compulsory pre- 
export inspections under economic liberalization process. 
2. The objective of the Quality Assurance which was sought to 
be achieved through "inspections" earlier is being achieved 
through "facilitation" in the form of Total Quality Management 
(TQM) consultancy, testing services, Human Resource 
Development (HRD) etc. 
3. The performance of several programmes/activities of the 
Committee such as Testing services, TQM Consultancy and 
Market Research has increased considerably in terms of 
diversity, utility, increased us ers and acceptability in the 
industry. 
4. The organization has been continuously improving and 
innovating its activities to match the industry's expectations. 
5. The internal revenue generated by the Committee through 
user charges has increased significantly, by putting the 
organization in the path of achieving financial self- 
sustainability in near future. 
6. The transformation and its management that took place in 
Textiles Committee has relevance and replicability to other

Accreditation of technical and educational institutions 
*289. SHRI PREM CHAND GUPTA: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that as per the report of the Comptroller and 
Auditor General (CAG) on the state of our Technical and Educational 
Institutions, none of the 171 Institutes audited by them could fulfil the  
AICTE requirements necessary for accreditation; and 
(b) if so, what are the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (DR. 
MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI): (a) and (b) As per Section 10 (k) of the 
AICTE Act, 1987, AICTE grants approval for starting new technical 
institutions and introducting new courses/increasing intake following a 
prescribed procedure. Accreditation of programmes is different from 
approval process. It is a process of quality assurance. AICTE has set 
up the National Board of Accreditation (NBA) in terms of Section 10(u) 
of the Act. The 171 Institutions test-checked in audit and mentioned in 
the Report of the Comptroller & Aud itor General of India (C&AG) were 
accorded approval by AICTE during the period 1997 -98 to 2001-02. 
As per the NBA guidelines, the minimum eligibility criteria for a 
programme to be considered for accreditation is that, at least two 
batches must have passed out from the concerned programme. As 
such, most of the institutions that were established during the period 
of report i.e. 1997-98 to 2001-02 were not eligible for accreditation. 
The response for accreditation in th e earlier years was poor due to 
lack of understanding and appreciation of the process involved. In 
order to encourage the institutions for getting their programmes 
accredited, AICTE has so far con ducted 49 awareness workshops 
and 14 training workshops.

Statement II 
Recommendations of Punnayya Committee 
1. Any additional resources genera ted by a university/institution may 
by kept in a separate fund to be utilised for furtherance of the 
objectives of the university/institution. 
2 UGC may provide a matching grant as an incentive to universities 
generating additional resources. 
3. There should be 100% income tax concession on all endowments 
and contributions made to the universities, and additional 
concessions to donors sponsoring  selected research projects in 
the universities. 
4. While universities should be en couraged to augment their 
resources for covering a larger proportion of costs of education 
than what prevails now, the in creased burden must be borne 
mainly by those who can afford. 
5. State or Government funding must continue to be an essential 
and mandatory requirement for support to higher education. The 
Government/State must continue to accept the major 
responsibility for funding the essential maintenance and 
developmental requirements of the universities.

specific objectives and to its pursuit of excellence, innovativeness, 
all-India character, and ability to provide access to weaker 
sections.

special inputs for strengthening the university's research 
infrastructure. 
8. Central university's may switch to appropriate mix of input funding 
and student funding systems, which may be standardised for 
comparable courses of study of UGC over a period of time. 
9. In regard to student funding, consideration of merit as well as 
social and economic backwardness should be taken into account. 
 
10. Quality, efficiency and innovativeness must be consciously 
rewarded and institutions failing to improve financial and academic 
discipline should face disincentives. 
11. The unit cost system of calculation of eligibility for grants should 
replace the existing incremental system which may by retained 
till the end of the current five-year plan period. 
12. From the Ninth Plan onwards, grants should be related to unit 
cost of activities as a rule except for new programmes for which 
unit costs are not determined, or would be difficult to determine. 
13. The Government must ensure that  the maintenance grant covers 
the wage bill of universities including periodical increases in 
increments, D.A. and other service charges. 
14. Heavy subsidies in many of the activities covered under 
maintenance grants, such as supply of electricity, transport, water 
supply etc. and in many other items have to be reviewed and 
reduced to a substantial extent so that the maintenance grant 
can be stabilized at a certain acceptable level.

activities would require periodical revision.

reviewed and curbed firmly wherever necessary.

Reducing Edible Oil Imports 
2078. SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether edible oil imports are projected to hit well over the 41 
per cent mark which reached in 2001 -2002; 
(b) whether edible oil imports is likely to rise more than the last year; 
(c) if so, the total edible oil imports made during the last year; 
(d) to what extent it will be more during the current year; 
(e) whether the Ministry had opposed to reduction of duty on imported 
palm oil and palmolein by the Finance Ministry; and 
(f) by when the efforts would be made to see that the production of 
edible oil in the country is improved, so that imports are reduced? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE 
(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) to (d) The import of edible 
oils during 2001-02 was 43.2 lakh metric tonnes and during 2002-03, 
about 42.66 lakh metric tonnes. There are no restriction on import other 
than the applicable rate of custom  duty. The gap between the domestic 
demand and domestic production of edible oils is met by imports. Thus, 
the quantum of import shall depend on domestic demand, domestic 
production and international prices of edible oils. 
(e) Yes, Sir. 
(f) The Government had set up a Technology Mission on Oilseeds 
in 1986 to increase the production and productivity of oilseeds and to 
reduce the import of edible oils. The Mission has launched a Centrally 
Sponsored Oilseeds Production Programme (OPP) in the country. 
Under the scheme financial assistance is provided on various inputs 
like production and distribution of seeds, distribution of seed minikits, 
distribution of improved farm implements, sprinkler sets, rhyzobium 
culture and micro nutrients etc. In order to disseminate the production 
technology amongst the farmers frontline demonstrations are organized 
by the I.C.A.R. and block demonstrations are organized by the State 
Deptt. of Agriculture. 
218 

[13 August, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
In case the weather conditions remain favourable during the coming 
years, the production of oilseeds is likely to increase from the present 
level which will reduce import of edible oils.

Ban on use of Endosulfan on Plantation Crops 
2082. SHRI H.K. JAVARE GOW DA: Will the Minister of 
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Endosulfan has been classified as 'highly 
hazardous' to health and banned in many countries; 
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that Endosulfan is still being used 
in the country particularly in Karnataka and Kerala on cashew plantations 
and has been linked to hundreds of cases of birth defects, psychiatric 
illness, cancer etc.; and 
(c) whether Government propose to ban the use of Endosulfan on 
plantation crops in the country, if so, the details thereof? 
221 

RAJYA  SABHA [13 August, 2003] 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN TH E MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE 
(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) As per "World Health 
Organisation (WHO) recommended classified by hazard", Endosulfan 
has been clasified as a "moderately hazardous" pesticide. It is 
reported to have been banned/severely restricted in 12 countries of 
the world because of the prevailing agro-climatic conditions and based 
on the specific requirements of those countries. 
(b) and (c) Endosulfan is being used in the country, except in 
Kerala, where the High Court of Kerala has, vide its interim order 
dated 12/08/2002, imposed a ban on the use of Endosulfan within 
the State of Kerala, pending a final decision by the Central Government 
on the report of the Expert Committe appointed by the Registration 
Committee constituted under Section 5 of the Insecticides Act, 1968 
to look into the report of National Institute of Occupational Health on 
its investigation of unusual illness allegedly reported by exposure to 
Endosulfan due to aerial spraying of Endosulfan over the cashew 
plantations in Padre Village of Kasa rgod District in N. Kerala with 
regard to higher prevalence of unusual diseases like mental 
retardation, congenital defect and abnormalities of re-productive 
system in children in the affected area. 
The Expert Committee has submitted its report to the Registration 
Committee and the Government is exam ining the report to arrive at a 
definite conclusion.

Production and procurement of potatoes 
†2086. SHRI LAJPAT RAI: 
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that production of potatoes is continuously 
increasing in the country for last decade; 
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that alongwith the increase in the 
production of potatoes, its cost of production is also increasing; 
(c) if so, the facts in this regard; and 
(d) whether it is also a fact that due to non-availability of proper 
arrangement for marketing of potato es, the potato growers are facing 
financial crises? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE 
(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) Yes, Sir. The potato 
production in the country has increased from 16.38 Million Tonnes during 
1991 -92 to 24.08 Million Tonnes in the year 2001 -02. 
(b) and (c) Yes, Sir. The cost of production is increasing with increase 
in cost of inputs, labour and also with adoption of improved technologies 
of production. As per estimates of Indian Council of Agriculture Research 
cost of production of table potato has increased from Rs. 105/ quintal 
during 2000-01 to Rs. 150/ quintal during 2001-02. 
(d) No, Sir. In order to provide remunerative prices to the farmers, 
the Government of India, on the request of States concerned, provide 
financial assistance through Market Intervention Scheme. During 2002- 
03 the Market Intervention scheme has been implemented in the States 
of Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal where, under the scheme, potato 
has been procured from farmers @ Rs. 190/quintal and Rs. 200/quintal 
respectively. 
Besides, with a view to create new outlets for utilizing the surplus 
potato production, the Government of Uttar Pradesh is providing 
assistance for transport of potato outside the State @ Rs. 250 per tonne.

[13 August, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA

Post production loss in agriculture sector 
†2087. SHRI KAPIL SIBAL: Will th e Minister of AGRICULTURE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that 25 percent of post production crop is 
assessed to be lost in agriculture sector of the country; 
(b) if not, facts in this regard; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that su ch loss could be minimized with 
the use of advanced technology; and 
(d) if so, facts in this regard an d how it compares with loss in 
agriculture sector at international level? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN TH E MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE 
(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) and (b) A Committee headed 
by Dr. V.G. Panse, in its report submitted in 1968, had estimated annual 
post harvest losses in the foodgrains in various stages at 9.33%.These 
included losses during threshing (1.68%), transportation (0.15%), 
processing (0.92%), rodents (2.50%), birds (0.85), insects (2.55%) and 
moisture (0.68%). A survey conducted by Directorate of Marketing and 
inspection, during 1973-74, had estimated post harvest losses in 
foodgrains to be about 5% out of which the storages losses were 
estimated at about 2.7%. A Joint survey conducted by the Indian 
Agricultural Statistics Research Institute and Indian Grain Storage 
Management and Research Institute during 1985—88 in Bulandshahar 
district of Uttar Pradesh and estimated total foodgrains losses at about 
4.12% due to different factors at various post harvest stages. A loss during 
storage and transit of foodgrains in the organized sector is however, less than 
0.5% and 1.5% respectively. 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
227 

RAJYA SABHA [13 August, 2003] 
The high level Committee on Cold Storage and Storage constituted 
by Department of Agriculture & Cooperation under the Chairmanship of 
Shri JNL Srivastava, Additional Secretary, in its Report of February 
1999 has estimated 25% to 30% post-harvest losses in horticultural 
produce depending upon the produce, season and the length of journey. 
(c) Yes, Sir. 
(d) In order to reduce losses to food-grains during the post harvest 
period, the Government of India had launched the Save Grain Campaign 
in 1969-70. The main thrust of activ ities of this Scheme is training, 
demonstration and publicity in the field of scientific storage of foodgrains 
at the farm level. Improvement of grain storage structure and 
popularization of scientific storage structures like metal bins, pucca 
kothis and RCC ring bins and other activities are carried out by the 
Save Grain Campaign for the benefit of farmers. 
Foodgrains stocks at commercial level are stored by various 
agencies on scientific lines duri ng which necessary prophylactic and 
curative measures are undertaken to reduce losses. 
In order to promote scientific storage facilites in rural areas and to 
prevent quantitative and qualitative loss es of the produce of the farmers, 
a Central Sector Scheme of construction/renovation of Rural Godowns 
titled "Grameen Bhandaran Yojana" is  being implemented in the country 
since 2001-2002. Under the Scheme, Central Government is providing 
investment subsidy to individual farmers, Self Help Group (SHG), 
Cooperatives, Corporations, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committees 
etc. Subsidy is provided @25% of the capital cost of  the project not 
exceeding Rs. 50.00 lakh for each st orage project through National Bank 
for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) and National 
Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC). A higher subsidy of 
33.3% of capital cost not exceeding Rs. 60.00 lakhs is  providing for 
beneficiaries belonging to SC/ST and for North-Eastern States and hilly 
areas. So far under the scheme, NABARD has sanctioned 995 projects 
with a capacity of 59.29 lakh tonnes. In addition, 1575 projects with a 
capacity of 7.42 lakh tonnes have been sanctioned by NCDC for 
construction of new rural godowns. 
A Capital investment Subsidy Scheme for construction of cold 
storage  is being  implemented by National Horticulture Board (NHB) 
228 

[13 August, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
through NABARD and NCDC to en hance the storage capacity for 
perishable commodities. Under the scheme, back-ended capital 
investment subsidy is provided to the eligible organisation @ 25% of 
the project cost not exceeding Rs. 50.00 lakh per project and @ 33.33% 
of the project cost upto a ceiling Rs. 60.00 lakh per project for North 
Eastern States. The Board has, so far, approved assistance of 
Rs. 208.17 crore under the scheme for creation of additional storage 
capacity of 31.79 lakh tonnes. 
No study has been conducted to compare post harvest losses in 
India with other countries.

contingency fund to help the drought, flood, thunder, landslide and snow

Governments. Financial assistance from Calamity Relief Fund (CRF) is

Growth of agriculture sector 
2101. SHRI ASHWANI KUMAR: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether any meaningful growth in the agriculture sector is 
expected in 2003-04, if so, what is the basis therefor; and 
(b) whether Central and State Government are contemplating fresh 
investments in the irrigation facilities to bring additional areas under 
agriculture and whether Government is considering crop diversification 
so as to make agriculture more remunerative for farmers? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE 
(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) The favourable monsoon 
rainfall has boosted the prospects of higher growth in the agriculture sector 
in 2003-04. The rainfall in the country as a whole in July 2003, which is 
agriculturally very active, was 107% of the Long Period Average (LPA). 
The cumulative rainfall during the period from 1st June to 30th July 2003 
was excess/normal in 32 out of 36 meteorological sub-divisions. 
244 

[13 August, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
(b) As irrigation is a State subject , all types of projects for creating 
Irrigation facilities are conceived, planned and implemented by the State 
Governments through the State sector plan investments according to 
the priority of the respective State Governments. The Planning 
Commission has approved an outlay of Rs. 92,144 crore in the Tenth 
Plan for Irrigation and Flood Control under State Plan. In addition to the 
State Plan allocation, Union Government is providing Central Loan 
Assistance (CLA) to the States under the Accelerated Irrigation Benefits 
Programme (AIBP) since 1996-97 for expeditious completion of on-going 
Irrigation Projects. An amount of Rs. 11,542 crore has been released 
upto March, 2003 as CLA to the States under AIBP. 
The basic aim of crop diversifi cation is to protect the natural 
resources viz soil health and to avoid over exploitation of ground water. 
Accordingly, the States are being advised to increase area under pulses 
and oilseeds crops. The Central Government has been announcing 
relatively higher Minimum Support Prices for pulses and oilseeds with a 
view to making crop diversification more remunerative for the farmers.

(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) to (c) According to the 
Ministry of Rural Development, a total quantity of 85.42 lakh MTs of 
foodgrains was released to the drought affected States of Andhra

recommendations of the Ministry of Agriculture. Foodgrains under the 
Special Component of the SGRY were released for taking up relief works

Increase in bird trade 
2120. PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ: Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT 
AND FORESTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that bird trade is on the increase; and 
(b) if so, what measures Government propose to take to check this 
menace? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT 
AND FORESTS (SHRI DILIP SINGH JUDEV): (a) and (b) The Wild Life 
(Protection) Act, 1972 prohibits trade in rare and endangered species of 
birds and regulates trade in other species of birds. Prevention and 
regulation of trade in birds is the responsibility of State Governments 
and there are no confirmed reports regarding increase in trade of birds. 
Government has, however, taken several measures in this regard.These 
are as follows: 
(i) Rare and endangered species of birds are included in the 
Schedule-I of Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972. Hunting of birds, 
disturbing or damaging their eggs or nests is a punishable offence. 
(ii) Trade in species of birds included in Schedule-IV is permitted 
with licence. Transportation of such birds is also regulated and 
no person can purchase, receive or acquire birds from a person 
not authorized to sale. 
(iii) Export of birds included in the Schedules of the Wild Life 
(Protection) Act, 1972 is prohib ited. Only six species of exotic 
birds are permitted for export. 
(iv) Government of India has set up Regional and Sub-regional offices 
for wild life preservation in major export and trade centres of the 
country to prevent smuggling of birds, wild animals and their 
products. 
(v) Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has been empowered under 
the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 to apprehend and prosecute 
269 

RAJYA SABHA [13 August, 2003] 
wild life offenders. Anti-poaching efforts are being coordinated with 
INTERPOL. 
(vi) Government of India seeks international co-operation under the 
provisions of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered 
Species of Wild Flora and Fauna (CITES) for control of illegal 
trade in wild life items.

2123. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTACHAR JEE: Will the Minister of 
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be pleased to state:

one horned rhinoceros is on the verge of collapse at the height of flood 
waves;

(c) whether Government are aware that the ravage by the floods 
has become an annual feature which destroys wildlife of the sanctuary 
regularly and if so, the short-term and long-term measures proposed to 
be taken to save the sanctuary from the flood waters causing havoc 
every year?f 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT 
AND FORESTS (SHRI DILIP SINGH JUDEV): 
(a) No, Sir. 
(b) Does not arise. 
(c) Annual flood is a natural phenomenon for a riverine ecosystem 
like Kaziranga National Park (KNP). However, at the time of high flood. 
278 

[13 August, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
which occurs in the park over a cycle of 7-8 years, some damage to 
both infrastructure and wildlife take s place. Various short-term and long- 
term measures taken to save the wildlife at KNP include:

Organisations and public for watch and ward and rescue of animals.

temporary camps wherever necessary.

Highway (NH) 37 and round-the-clock monitoring the movement of

Objectives of National and State Women's Commissions 
[Extracts of section 10(1) of National Commission for Women Act, 
1990 on functions of National Commission for Women] 
10. Function of the Commission .—(1) The Commission shall 
perform all or any of the following functions, namely:— 
(a) investigate and examine all matters relating to the safeguards 
provided for women under the Constitution and other laws; 
(b) present to the Central Government, annually and at such other 
times as the Commission may deem fit, reports upon the working 
of those safeguards; 
301 

RAJYA  SABHA [13 August, 2003] 
(c) make in such reports recomm endations for the effective 
implementation of those safeguards for improving the conditions 
of women by the Union or any State; 
(d) review, from time to time, the existing provisions of the Constitution 
and other laws affecting women and recommend amendments 
thereto so as to suggest remedial legislative measures to meet 
any lacunae, inadequacies or shortcomings in such legislations; 
(e) take up the cases of violation of the provisions of the Constitution 
and of other laws relating to women with the appropriate 
authorities; 
(f) look into complaints and take suo moto notice of matters relating 
to— 
(i) deprivation of women's rights; 
(ii) non-implementation of laws  enacted to provide protection 
to women and also to achieve the objective of equality and 
development. 
(iii) non-compliance of policy decisions, guidelines or 
instructions aimed at mitigating hardships and ensuring 
welfare and providing relief to women and take up the 
issues arising out of such matters with appropriate 
authorities; 
(g) call for special studies or inves tigations into specific problems or 
situations arising out of discrimination and atrocities against 
women and identify the constraints so as to recommend strategies 
for their removal; 
(h) undertake promotional and educational research so as to suggest 
ways of ensuring due representation of women in all spheres 
and identify factors responsible for impending their advancement, 
such as, lack of access to housin g and basic services, inadequate 
support services and technologies for reducing drudgery and 
occupational health hazards and for increasing their productivity; 
(i) participate and advise on the planning process of socio-economic 
development of women; 
302 

[13 August, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
(j) evaluate the progress of the development of women under the 
Union and any State; 
(k) inspect or cause to be inspected a jail, remand home, women's 
institution or other place of cust ody where women are kept as 
prisoners or otherwise, and take up with the concerned authorities 
for remedial action, if found necessary; 
(I) fund litigation involving issues affecting a large body of women; 
(m) make periodical reports to  the Government on any matter 
pertaining to women and in particular various difficulties under 
which women toil; 
(n) any other matter which may be referred to it by the Central 
Government.

2195. SHRI SAN JAY NIRUPAM: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be

of the Konkan Rail route in Maharashtra; and

Railways? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
(SHRI BANDARU DATTATRAYA): (a) an d (b) Various safety hazards in 
tunnels are related to ventilation, trank maintenance, boulder fall, 
darkness, drainage, refuge communication and fire. Indentified tunnels 
are provided with ballast-less track to take care of track maintenance 
problems in long tunnels (more than 4 kms.) and selected lengths of the 
tunnels are provided with concrete lining, shotcreting, rock bolting to 
support weak areas. All the tunnel s are annually inspected and loose 
scaling is carried out at the requi red locations. Ventilation has been 
provided in tunnels longer than 4 kms. to ensure proper quality of air 
and to exhaust the smoke emitted by the locomotive. It  also prevents 
suffocation if the train stops inside the tunnel. State of art monitoring 
and control systems are installed. Lighting has been provided in the 
identified tunnels to assist passengers to evacute if necessary. All trains 
on Konkan Railways are vestibuled. Side drains have been provided for 
the passage of the water with cover on the top to act as pathway and 
refuges have been provided in the tunnels for men and trolley to 
accomodate themselves when the train is passing. Communication

2199. SHRIMATI SARLA MAHESH WARI: Will the Minister of

(b) why does Railways allow tea/ coffee vendors to carry burning

(c) why there is no fire extinguishers existed in all compartments in 
Indian Railway even after many incidents of fire reported in the past? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
(SHRI BANDARU DATTATRAYA): (a) Indi an Railways are continuously 
upgrading the fire retardant properties of each and every material used in

flammability and fire retardance properties of various material 
utilized in manufacture of Indian Railway Coaches. 
* Adoption of naval Specification (NCD 1409,1410 and 1411) and 
FAR (Airline Safety) specification for toxicity and smoke level 
emission for upholstery, fabric and curtains.

passengers from carrying any inflammable or explosive materials.

extinguishers are not provided in other unmanned coaches as safe 
keeping of these costly items cannot be ensured.

Steel exports to China 
2223. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY SIRIGIREDDY: 
SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA RAO: 
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that China opened its doors for importing 
Steel from India and Other countries of the world; 
(b) if so, whether Beijing has issued any import quota for us; 
(c) if so, for how long this quota system is valid; 
(d) the total potential of steel India can export to China before quota 
system closes; and 
(e) how Government are planning to grab the opportunity of exporting 
steel to China? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF STEEL 
(SHRI BRAJ KISHORE TRIPATHY): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) and (c) In May 2002, China initiated safeguard investigations 
against import of various categories of steel from several countries, 
including India. In November 2002 the investigations were completed 
361 

RAJYA SABHA [13 August, 2003] 
and final safeguard measures in the form of quotas on five categories 
of steel items were imposed with additional tariff in case the imports 
exceed the relevant quota. These m easures would be in place for the 
next two and a half years. However, these measures do not apply to 
India. 
(d) In accordance with the WTO ru les China has exempted the 
developing countries, including India from the safeguard measures. 
However, the exemption is subject to the condition that import share of 
a developing country in a particular category should not exceed 3% of 
China's total import volume in that category. 
(e) A delegation led by the Minister of State for Steel visited China 
from May 18-23, 2002. The purpose of the visit was to explore 
opportunities of cooperation in the Iron and Steel sector. At times, the 
public sector undertakings under the Ministry of Steel and delegations 
to China to promote exports, source raw materials and explore areas of 
co-operation. Apart from these Ministry and PSU initiatives, the Embassy 
of India, Beijing has also identified products which are in demand under 
the Harmonised System Code 72 (Iron and Steel) in the Chinese market 
and the necessary information has been forwarded to the concerned 
Indian Chambers of Commerce/Export  Councils and industry players 
active in the field of Iron and Steel. The Indian Steel Alliance, working 
under the aegis of the confederation of India Industry (Cll), has already 
initiated talks with the Chinese government and steel companies in China 
to increase trade between the two countries. 
The Ministry is thus actively involved in various promotional efforts 
in consultation with the industry and their Associations. The Government 
is fully discharging its role as a facilitator in a liberalised environment 
and helping the industry to adequately exploit the market potential.

Uniform Civil Code 
*310.  SHRI P. PRABHAKAR REDDY: 
SHRI N.K. PREMACHANDRAN: 
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Supreme Court of India has underlined the need for 
enactment of a Uniform Civil Code for all sections of people in the 
country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) Government's reaction thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF LAW  AND JUSTICE (SHRI ARUN JAITLEY): 
(a) and (b) The Supreme Court of India in its judgement delivered on 
384 

[13 August, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
21.7.2003 in the matter of John Vallamattom Vs Union of India has made 
certain observations in respect of the need for enactment of a Uniform 
Civil Code. The relevant extracts fr om the judgement are annexed as 
Statement. (See below). 
(c) There is no decision taken by the Government to frame a Uniform 
Civil Code. 
Statement 
Relevant extracts from the judgement delierved by the 
Supreme Court of India 
The Supreme Court of India in its judgement delivered on 21.7.2003 
in th matter of John Vallamattom Vs Union of India has observed in para 
44 of the said judgement as under:- 
"44. Before I part with the case I would like to state that article 44 
provides that the State shall end eavour to secure for the citizens a 
Uniform Civil Code throughtout the territory of India. The  aforesaid 
provision is based on the premise that there is no necessary 
connection between religious and personal law in a civilized society. 
Article 25 of the Constitution confers freedom of conscience and 
fee profession, practice and propagation of the religion.The aforesaid 
two provisions viz. articles 25 and 44 show that the former guarantees 
religious freedom whereas the latter divests religion from social 
relations and personal law. It is no matter of doubt that marriage, 
succession and the like matters of a secular character cannot be 
brought within the guarantee enshrined under articles 25 and 26 of 
the Constitution. Any legislation which bring succession and the 
like matters of secular character within the ambit of articles 25 & 26 
is a suspect legislation. Although it is doubtful whether the American 
doctrine of suspect legislation is followed in this country. In 
Smt. Sarla Mudgal, President, Kalyani and others Vs Union of India 
and others (1995 (3) SGC 635), it was held that marriage, sucession 
and like matters of secu lar character cannot be brought within the 
guarantee enshrined under articles 25 & 26 of the Constitution. It is 
a matter of regret that article 44 of the Constitution has not been 
given effect to. Parliament is still to step in for framing a common 
civil code in the country. A common civil code will help the cause of 
385 

RAJYA  SABHA [13 August, 2003] 
national integration by removi ng the contradictions based on 
ideologies".

*311. SHRI EKANATH K.  THAKUR: Will the Minister of HEALTH 
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware of the fact that according to the 
World Health Organisation's report, India has the highest number of TB 
cases in the world; 
(b) whether it is a fact that though the country is credited with most 
rapidly developing free DOTS (Directly Observed Therapy) programme 
in the world, only 55 per cent Indians were covered by DOTS in 2002; 
and 
(c) if so, the steps Government propose to take to cover more Indians 
under DOTS? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) to (c) Yes, Sir. India accounts 
for nearly one-third of Global TB burden. It is estimated that every year 
about 2 million new cases are occurri ng in the country of which about 
50% are sputum positive, which are infectious cases of TB. However, 
the incidence of TB in India estima ted by WHO at 178 cases per lakh 
population is lower than the rate of incidence in many high ranking 
countries but due to the large population size in India the actual number 
of patients in the country is larger. 
DOTS coverage is being rapidly expanded in the country. From 
20 million coverage in 1998, about 700 million population has been 
covered at present. It is envisaged to cover 850 million population by 
2004 and the entire country by 2005 under the revised strategy. 
750 million population of several Stat es will be covered under World 
Bank Assisted Project. Andhra Prades h, Orissa and Haryana are to be 
covered with assistance from DFID, DANIDA and USAID respectively. 
The three new States of Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand & Uttaranchal and 
balance population of UP and Bihar, are to be covered by assistance 
from the Global Funds for AIDS, TB and Malaria (GFATM).

population, facilities for diagnosis by sputum microscopy have been 
decentralized at places near to be  patients and stre ngthened. Drugs

all general hospitals, private practitioners and NGOs in the programme.

has been set aside by the High Court of Kerala. The State Government 
has filed a Special Leave Petition against this judgement in the Hon'ble 
Supreme Court. Several other petitions have been filed by private 
institutions in the Hon'ble Supreme Court challenging the validity of the 
regulations framed by the State Governments and also the guideline of 
Central Government dated 14.5.2003 vis-a-vis the judgement of the 
Hon'ble Court dated 31.10.2002. All these petitions have been tagged 
together and were recently heard by  Five-Judge Constitution Bench of 
the Hon'ble Supreme Court. 
Before the Five-Judge Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme 
Court of India some of the Private Institutions have submitted that as 
per the judgement of the Hon'ble Court dated 31.10.2002, they have 
complete autonomy in the matter of admission of students. As the 
acceptance of such a contention would lead to multiplicity of entrance 
389 

RAJYA SABHA [13 August, 2003] 
examinations; clashing of examina tion dates and undue hardships to 
students and their parents, the Central Government have submitted a 
proposal before the Hon'ble Court for evolving a scheme to conduct a 
combined All-India Entr ance Examination through a suitable agency for 
selection of candidates for admission to various Government and private 
medical colleges in different States. The proposed scheme would also 
allow sufficient flexibility to the Stat es/Medical colleges in choosing the 
candidates from amongst the candidates who qualify the examination 
while ensuring the primacy of merit in selection of candidates even 
against the seats filled up by the Management. The hearing before the 
Hon'ble Court in this matter has concluded and the judgement is 
reserved.

*315. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND

contraceptive methods is being diluted and more emphasis is being

NACO, is implementing a comprehensive National AIDS Control 
Programme across the country through State AIDS Control Societies. 
The World Health Organization (WHO) , in their Global Programme on 
AIDS (GPA), popularized the ABC approach which is being followed in 
over 150 countries, and is by now,  an internationally accepted media 
and program strategy. It is based on the belief that HIV is a problem 
with a solution. It contemplates bringing about behaviour change within 
high risk behaviours that include, but are not limited to: 
Abstinence and/or delayed sexual debut;

Being faithful to, and developing fidelity towards single partner 
relationships; and 
Condom promotion for protection. 
There is no dilution in the strategy for containing HIV/AIDS. We

accordance with societal norms, soci o-cultural milieus the stage of the 
HIV/AIDS epidemic and key target populations.

our IT professionals and service providers. Our keen interest in the 
Information Technology se ctor in providing more access for our service 
providers and IT professionals in markets abroad and the advantages 
that would accrue to othe r countries throu gh liberalisation of this sector

auction system in tea;

(c) the progress, if any, achieved as a result thereof; 
(d) whether Government have noticed that several tea estates have 
been closed and tens of thousands of workers were thrown out of 
employment resulting in starvation deaths; and

and State-wise? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE 
AND INDUSTRY (SHRI CHENNAMANENI VIDYASAGAR RAO): (a) 
Concerned with the fall in auction prices of tea and such fall not getting 
reflected in the retail prices, a study of the primary marketing system 
for tea was conducted through M/s A.F. Ferguson & Co. The major 
recommendations of the Ferguson Committee with respect to the auction 
system, include discouraging divisibility of lots and proxy bidding, fixing 
maximum sample limits, defining lot sizes in terms of weight rather than 
volume, introduction of ex-estate sale and electronising the bidding 
process in the auction centres. 
(b) and (c) Based on the recommendations of M/s A.F. Ferguson & 
Co. the Government notified the Tea Marketing Control Order, 2003 on 
01.01.2003 in replacement of the TMCO 1984. Necessary directions 
regarding the Changes in the auction rules were issued by the Tea Board 
for a more transparent and effici ent price discovery mechanism. 
Government has also approved implementation of an Information 
Technology based Information Dissemination Plan for the tea industry 
which covers electronising the tea auction centers in India.

Export of commercial services 
2262. SHRI R.S. GAV AI: Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
(a) the present status so far India's exports of commercial services 
is concerned; and 
(b) the details of the measures taken by Government to increase 
export of commercial services? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE 
AND INDUSTRY (SHRI SATYABRATA MOOKHERJEE): (a) As per the 
latest WTO report, the value of exports of commercial services made by 
India in 2002 is placed at US$ 20.7 billion constituting 1.3% of the world 
exports of commercial services. The rate of growth of export of 
commercial services in 2002 over the previous year was 8% in dollar 
terms. 
(b) Under the Exim Policy, the Government has formulated a scheme 
wherein Service Providers have been allowed duty free credit entitlement 
for import of spares, office equipment and furniture, professional equipment 
and consumables, except the agriculture and dairy products. The en titlement 
would be equivalent to 10% of the average foreign exchange earned by them 
in the preceding three licensing years excepting for the Service Providers in the 
Tourism Sector. The entitlement in the case of hotels of the category of three 
star and above and those related to the Tourism Sector, registered with the 
Department of Tourism, 
428 

[13 August, 2003] RAJYA    SABHA 
would be 5% of the average foreig n exchange earned by them in the 
preceding three licensing years. The scheme will cover only those Service 
Providers who have an average fo reign exchange earning of over 
Rs. 10 lakhs in the preceding three licensing years.

COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:

towards upgradation of trade and commerce with the neighbouring countries 
through N.E. corridor showing location-wise infrastructure developed so far 
and the achievements made:

for promotion of border trade: and

connecting N.H. 38 through Myanmar?

to the visit of the Hon'ble Prime Minister, the Central Government has 
set up an Empowered Committee on Promotion of Trade and Exports in 
North East and Sikkim.The important steps taken to upgrade trade and 
commerce with the neighbouring countries through the North East region 
are as under: 
(i) Four border townships at Zokhawtha (Mizoram). Moreh (Manipur). 
Dawki (Meghalaya) and Sutarkhandi (Assam) have been identified 
for development of trade related infrastructure and an amount of 
Rs. 16.29 crores has been sanctioned. 
(ii) A trade-cum-exhibition centre has been sanctioned at Guwahati 
for which an amount of Rs. 13.40 crores has been sanctioned. 
(iii) 'APEDA has sanctione d four reefer vans in the North East region

any disease is the responsibility of the respective State Governments, 
Government of India provides technical support to the States by sending 
expert teams to the affected stat es for guidance. During the recent 
outbreak of viral encephalitis in Andhra Pradesh, support has also been

addition to the insecticides and larv icides already provided under the

of contagious diseases are prevalent in the country. A part from various 
steps taken to strengthen the public health system in order to ensure 
early detection and treatment of diseases at the point of first contact, a 
number of focused disease control programmes are being run by the 
Government for identification and control of various diseases like 
Tuberculosis, HIV/AIDS, Leprosy and surveillance of other communicable

The National Surveillance Progra mme for Communicable Diseases 
was launched as a pilot programme in 1997-98 in 5 districts with a view 
to strengthen the disease surveill ace system of various communicable 
diseases so that early warning signals of outbreaks are recognized and 
appropriate follow-up action is initiated.The programme is implemented 
through the existing health infrastrcture and surveillance system involving 
training of medical and para-medical personnel, upgradation of 
laboratories and improvement in communication system.The programme 
is currently implemented in 101 districts. Under the 10th Five Year Plan, 
a Project Implementation Plan is en visaged to strengthen the existing 
surveillance system at the District, State and National levels. 
The Revised National TB Control Programme (RNTCP) has been 
in operation in the country since 1952. To achieve a cure rate of 85% of 
new sputum positive cases and to detect at least 70% of such cases, 
Revised National T.B. Control Programme (RNTCP) which is Directly 
Observed Treatment—Short Course (DOTS) Strategy, is implemented 
in the country in a phased manner. Under the Programme, 100% 
requirement of anti-TB drugs and Binocular Microscopes are provided 
as commodity grant by the Centre to all the States/UTs for undertaking 
various activities for implementation of RNTCP, Cash assistance is 
released to States/District TB Societies. The Programme is regorously 
monitored through quarterly performance reports. 
In order to combat the problem of AIDS, Government has launched 
a comprehensive AIDS prevention and control programme, which is a 
100% centrally sponsored scheme implemented in all States/UTs 
through States/UTs' AIDS Control Societies. The main components of 
the Programme consist of:- 
• Reducing the spread of HIV in groups at high risk by identification 
of target population and providing peer counseling, condom 
451

promotion, and treatment of sexually transmitted infections. 
• Preventive intervention for the general population by Information, 
Education and Communication (IEC) and awareness compaign, 
provision of voluntary testing and counseling, safe blood 
transfusion services and prevention of occupational exposure. 
• Providing financial assistance for opportunistic infections home 
and community based care. 
• Strengthening effectiveness and technical managerial, financial 
sustainability at National, State, and Municipal levels. 
• Promoting collaboration amongst public, private and voluntary 
sector. 
For the elimination of Leprosy in the country, the Government of 
India is implementing National Leprosy Eradication Programme (NLEP), 
a 100% Centrally sponsored Scheme  with the objec tive of achieving 
the elimination of Leprosy, i.e. prevalence of less than 1 case per 10,000 
population at national level by the year 2005.

National Health Fund 
2291. SHRI SATISH PRADHAN: Will th e Minister of HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have constituted a National Health Fund 
to provide medical assistance to the helpless and poor people; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) whether Government are considering to introduce community 
based Universal Health Insurance Scheme for the poor people so that 
all sections of the society get quality health care facility? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) On the recommendation of the 
Department related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Human 
Resources Development, a National Illness Assistance Fund was set 
up in 1997. Its name has now been changed as "Rashtriya Arogya 
Nidhi" vide Government's Resolution No. W. 11011/2/2003-NIAF dated 
8.4.2003. 
(b) The Rastriya Arogya Nidhi provides financial assistance to 
patients, living below poverty line, suff ering from life threatening diseases, 
to receive medical treatment at any of the super-speciality Hospitals/ 
Institute or other Government Hospitals. The financial assistance is 
released in the form of 'one time grant'. 
(c) A 'Universal Health Insurance Scheme' was launched on 
countrywide basis by the Prime Minister on 14th July, 2003. 
Treatment of foreign patients 
2292. SHRI SHAHID SIDD IQUI: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether in the light of a number of patients from foreign countries 
wanting to avail health care facilities in India, Government have 
conducted a survey on further development of these opportunities; 
(b) whether Government have taken any steps to develop Medical 
Tourism which is expected to fetch 10 thousand crore additional revenue 
by the year 2012; and 
457 

RAJYA SABHA [13 August, 2003] 
(c) whether Government are preparing a joint programme with the 
Ministries of Tourism an Civil Aviation to bring more tourists in the health 
sector? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) to (c) The Government is aware 
that certain hospitals in India are offering quality medical care in areas 
such as Cardiac Surgery, Ophthalmol ogy etc. at a fraction of the cost 
incurred in developed countries. A report commissioned by the 
Confederation of Indian Industry in association with M/s Mskinsey has 
outlined the great potential for medical tourism in India due to a strong 
value preposition on cost, quality and services. 
It is the endeavor of the government to provide quality medical care 
to all citizens and also to promote the use of quality facilities for treatment 
of needy patients from other countries. For this purpose, India is one of the 
few countries to have given a commitment for allowing foreign investments 
in the hospital sector with a cap on foreign equity to the extent on 51%. 
Foreign equity investment of upto 100% is allowed with FIPB clearance in the 
Hospital Sector. A new scheme has been introduced as per the new EXIM 
policy which provides for duty free imports equivalent of 10% of average 
foreign exchange earning in preced ing three years by health service 
providers. 
It is felt that as more and more investment comes into the hospital 
sector both from private and public sources, India's potential in medical 
tourism will continue to expand.

Causes of death of pregnant women 
†2294. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) the reasons behind the death of pregnant women alongwith the 
number of deaths as a result thereof during the year 2002-03 till June 
this year; 
(b) whether there has been any increas e or decrease in such cases 
during the last two years; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) Based on the data provided by 
the Sample Registration System-1998, of the Registrar General of India, 
the major causes of deaths of pregnent women are: 
1. Direct Causes: Haemorrhage, in fections, Obstructed Labour, 
Unsafe Abortion, Toxemia of Pregnancy etc. 
2. Indirect Causes: Anaemia, Viral Heapatitis, Tuberculosis and 
Malaria. 
In addition to the above, socio economic causes like early age of 
marriage, adolescent pregnancy, low status of women, low level of female 
education, lack of access to health  services, gender bias and economic 
dependency also contribute to maternal mortality. 
The exact number of cases of deaths of pregnant women in the 
country in the year 2002-03 till June, is not available. The Sample 
Registration System as mentioned above reported the maternal mortality 
ratio as 407 for the year 1998. Based on this, it is estimated the above. 
1.1 lakh women in India die every year due to cause related to pregnancy 
and childbirth.

2299. SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD: W ill the Minister of HEALTH 
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government's attention has been drawn to the warning 
of the World Health Organisation that non-communicable diseases would 
account for over 55 per cent of deaths in India by 2020; 
(b) if so, whether Government have taken any steps to creat 
awareness among the public for a dopting the basic life style changes 
as recommended by WHO;

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN TH E MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) to (d) Yes, Sir. As the major 
non-communicable disease like Diab etes, Cardio-Vascular Diseases 
(CVD), Cancer etc. are life style related diseases, it is very important to 
adopt preventive lifestyle interventio n measures such as healthy diet, 
increased physical activity, avoidan ce to tobacco and stress, weight 
reduction etc. These interventio ns are being emphasized through 
information, education & communication (IEC) activities of the 
Government including through Central Health Education Bureau (CHEB). 
Health Melas are also organized thro ughout the country from time to 
time in which various Central and State Organizations participate and 
disseminate health awareness messages. 
In addition, the National Cancer Control Programme (NCCP) has an 
IEC component for creating awareness, which is implemented through the 
District Cancer Control Programme, the Non-Governmental Organizations 
and the Regional Cancer Centres, Cancer awareness programmes are 
telecast through Kalyani Tele Magazine of Prasar Bharti in 8 States.

manner. The State of Delhi is full y covered under revised strategy since 
year 2001. RNTCP project in Delh i has reported treatment success 
rate of more than 80%, which means that more than 8 out of every 10

during the XXth Annual Conference of In dian Society of Medical Statistics 
at Indian Council of Medical Research, New Delhi on 19-22, December,

fertility and family planning in 21 slums out of 218 slums in Varanasi of

in the status of Contraceptive Prevalence Rate. The Contraceptive 
Prevalence Rate in the country has improved from 40.6% to 48.2% in 
total, from 51.0% to 58.2% in urban areas and from 36.9% to 44.7% in 
rural areas.

(b) if so, how many cases of corruption have been brought to

Act to deal with the corruption in judiciary by amending the statute; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR LAW AND JUSTICE (SHRI P.C. 
THOMAS):, (a) and (b) Allegations of deviant behaviour involving acts of 
corruption and moral turpitude, against some members of Judicial Service 
of the States and some Judges of High Courts have come to the notice of 
the Government. However, under article 235 of the Constitution of India, 
the administrative control over the members of Subordinate Judicial 
Service vests with the concerned High C ourt. Further, in exercise of powers 
conferred under proviso to article 309 read with article 233 and 234 of the 
Constitution, the State Government frames rules and regulations in 
consultation with the High Court. As regards scandals involving judicial 
officers of District/Sessions Courts, the disciplinary control lies with the 
concerned High Court. Under these circumstances the Central 
Government is not maintaining a data on this. 
(c) and (d) No, Sir. The Judges Inquiry Act is to regulate the 
procedure for the investigation and proof of the misbehaviour or 
incapacity of a Judge of  the Supreme Court or High Court and for the 
presentation of an address by Parliame nt to the President and for matters 
connected therewith. Subordinate Judiciary does not come under the 
purview of this Act. However, the Constitution (Ninety-Eighth 
Amendment) Bill, 2003 propose to vest the power of inquiry into cases 
of misconduct or such deviant behaviour of a Judge, other than those 
calling for his removal, in the National Judicial Commission.The Bill has 
already been introduced in the Parliament.

Beggars in Delhi 
2362. SHRI RAJU PARMAR: Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE 
AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware of  the fact that begging is an 
organized racket in Delhi; 
(b) if so, the action taken by Government to completely remove 
begging from the inter-sections and other hot spots of NCT of Delhi; 
and 
(c) whether Government have ever  launched a drive to punish 
beggars during the last two years, and if so, the reasons for continuation 
of various gangs of beggars operating in Delhi? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SOCIAL 
JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT (SHRI NAGMANI): (a) to (c) As per 
the information furnished by the Department of Social Welfare, 
Government of NCT of Delhi, there is no authentic report to suggest 
incidence of begging through any organized racket in Delhi. 
Begging is an offence under Section 4 of the Bombay Prevention 
of Begging Act, 1959. Regular anti-begging raids are conducted in 
association with the Delhi Police under the said Act. Special drives and 
anti-begging awareness campaigns are also undertaken from time to 
522 

[13 August, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
time for apprehending beggars at public places and mobilizing public 
opinion against giving alms. After apprehension beggars are produced 
at a special court presided over by a metropolitan magistrate and are 
sent to custodial institutions for beggars where various services are 
provided for weaning them away from beggary and making them self- 
reliant. During th years 2001-02 and 2002-03, 3776 beggars were 
apprehended out of which 1788 beggars were convicted. However, 
there is constant influx of beggars from other States making it difficult 
to completely remove them from public places.

2363. PROF. M. SANKARALINGAM: Will the Minister of SOCIAL 
JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware that  there is an increase in the 
number of drug abusers in the country; 
(b) what is the status of such drug abusers; and 
(c) what elaborate steps have been taken by Government to stop 
drug abusers from spreading their ugly tentacles in rural parts of the 
country? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SOCIAL 
JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT (SHRI NAGMANI): (a) Various 
surveys and reports indicate an increasing trend of drug abuse amongst 
certain vulnerable sections of the society. 
(b) and (c) While the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance 
is administering Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) 
Act (as amended in the year 2001) for effectively regulating the 
availability of illicit drugs in the country, the Ministry of Social Justice & 
Empowerment is implementing a Scheme entitled "Scheme for 
Prevention of Alcoholism and Substance (Drugs) Abuse" wherein Non- 
Government Organisations are provided with financial support for 
awareness generation, counselling se rvices, treatment and rehabilitation 
of such drugs abusers. In addition,  NGOs are also being funded for 
deaddiction Campus for treatment of addicts in community settings, 
especially in rural ar eas. Around 450 programm es are being funded 
all over the country, including rural areas with an annual allocation of 
Rs. 25.50 crores for treatment and rehabilitation of drug abusers.

RAJYA  SABHA [13 August, 2003] 
Funds to Urban Local Bodies of Uttar Pradesh 
†2377. SHRI MUNAVVAR HASAN: Will the Minister of URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have taken any steps to strengthen the 
urban local bodies of Uttar Pradesh; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the funds released to the urban local bodies of the State during 
the last three years, year-wise; and 
(d) the results achieved therefrom? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION (SHRI PON. 
RADHAKRISHNAN): (a) to (d) As per entry 5 of the State List of Seventh 
Schedule of the Constitution, 'local Government' is a State Subject. In 
view of this, it is for the State Government to take necessary steps to 
strengthen urban local bodies. The Ministry of Urban Development & 
Poverty Alleviation have not released any fund to urban local bodies of 
Uttar Pradesh for the purpose of strengthening urban local bodies. 
However, the Government of India have taken a number of steps to 
strengthen urban local bodies (ULBs)  of the country. As the first and 
foremost measure, the Constitution (74th Amendment) Act, 1992 was 
enacted and all the States have amended their Municipal Laws to devolve 
adequate functional and financial powers to municipalities in conformity 
with the provisions enshrined in the above Act. 
States have constituted State Finance Commissions to review the 
financial position of the municipalities and make recommendations to 
the State Government with regard to taxation; sharing of taxes between 
the State Government and Local Gove rnment; principles for governing 
grant-in-aid; and measures for improving the financial position of urban 
local bodies. 
Suitable amendment has also been made to Article 280 of the 
Constitution to make it mandatory that the Central Finance Commission 
shall, inter-alia, make specific recommendations with regard to measures 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
550 

[13 August, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
that are needed to augment the reso urces of a State with a view to 
supplementing the resources of municipalities in the States on the basic 
of the recommendations made by the State Finance Commission. 
Besides, the Govt.of India have initiated needed urban sector reforms 
with a view to strengthening ULBs both in terms of capacity building and 
good financial management. The urban sector reforms include the 
following components: 
• Setting up of Urban Reforms Incentive Fund to provide reform- 
linked assistance to States. 
• Tax-free Municipal Bonds for issue by urban local bodies for 
portable water supply, sewerage of sanitation, drainage, solid 
waste management, roads/bridges/flyovers, and urban transport. 
In addition, the Central Government has announced tax exemption 
in case of bonds issued by municipal/local governments for raising 
resources for urban infrastructure. 
• Urban Development Plans and Implementation Guidelines issued 
in 1996. These guidelines emphasize for innovative approaches 
for fiscal resource mobilization, rationalization of subsidies, 
commercial orientation of urban development plans. 
• Municipal accounting system serves as an effective management 
tool for financial activities of urban local bodies, promote effective 
and timely decision making process and facilitate better 
accountability and transparency. To bring about needed reforms 
in the municipal accounting system, a Task Force was set up to 
suggest accounting and budget formats for urban local bodies. 
The Task Force in its report has recommended for budget and 
accounting formats for ULBs with  appropriate codification and 
classification of budget and acco unt heads. The report of the 
Task Force has been circulated to all States for implementation 
in April, 2003. 
• Government with the objective of simplification and rationalization 
of property tax, which is considered as one of the buoyant sources 
of revenue for urban local bodies, have issued Guidelines to all 
State Governments in 1998. Uttar Pradesh is one of the States 
which is in the process of implementing property tax reforms.

JE posted in the area. 
(b) Does not arise. 
(c) The number of surprise checks c onducted by the officers of the

Homeless SC & ST families in Urban and Rural Areas 
†2380. SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI : Will the Minister of URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of SC and ST families residing in urban areas, rural 
areas and in metropolitan cities as per the data collected by the National 
Building Organisation, which do not have their own houses/ 
accommodation facility; 
(b) out of these, the number of such families in Madhya Pradesh 
and Maharashtra; and 
(c) the steps being taken by Government to provide housing facilities 
to such families? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN  THE MINISTRY OF URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION (SHRI PON 
RADHAKRISHNAN): (a) and (b) National Building Organisation does 
not collect the information on Sc heduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes 
houseless families in rural/urban areas and Metros. 
(c) One of the aims of the National Housing & Habitat Policy 1998 is 
to meet the special needs of Sc heduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes. 
However, since Housing is a State subject it is the responsibility of the 
State Governments to draw up housing schemes for the Scheduled 
Castes/Scheduled Tribes families.

centrally sponsored scheme called Valmiki Ambedkar Awas Yojana

living below poverty line in urban slums. The scheme has also a 
component known as Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan (NBA) for the construction

India subsidy of 50% and the balance 50% to be arranged by the State

as per the guidelines. An allocation of Rs. 296.68 lakhs during the year

On issues arising out of the 54th Report of the Public Accounts Committee 
(2003-2004) which was Laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha on the 
6th August, 2003 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, on August 7, Shri Suresh 
Pachouri had raised the issue in the Question Hour demanding urgent 
discussion on the Government having not made available CVC's Report and 
complete documents to the PAC whose 54th Report was laid on the Table 
of the House the previous day (August 6). 
In the afternoon of August 7, this matter was taken up in the 
.meeting of BAC. Some Members drew attention to the fact that in the 
Report, PAC had observed that the Ministry of Defence had refused to 
supply the CVC Report on the defenc e deals and that in the absence of 
such a vital document, PAC had regretted its inability to give findings on the 
defence procurement transactions repo rted in the C&AG's Report. Some 
other Members stated that there was no CVC report on OP Vijay (Army) and 
PAC appeared to have raised an uncalled for controversy about non- 
submission of a report which, really, did not exist. It was, therefore, felt that 
the key issue was to ascertain the facts about the investigation conducted

or Report made by the CVC on defence transactions relating to 
'procurement for OP Vijay (Army)' and that I, as Chairman, may go through 
the relevant papers relating to the 54th Report of the PAC, ascertain 'facts 
and take a decision. The BAC was also apprised of the letter received from 
Minister of Defence seeking time to make a statement in the House to 
clarify the issues raised in the Report of the PAC. 
The matter was raised in the House on the 8th morning seeking a 
discussion on the notice moved by Shri Suresh Pachouri for suspension of 
Question Hour under Rules 267 and 38 and "to initiate a discussion on the 
refusal of Government to provide relevant documents and information to 
PAC pertaining to Operation Vijay". I had apprised the House that, as 
discussed at the meeting of the BAC he ld the previous afternoon, I would 
go through the relevant papers to asce rtain the facts and then apprise the 
House accordingly. 
Hon. Members, the PAC, in para 6 of its Report, had stated that 
they had requested the Ministry of Defence to make available the CVC 
Report on "Defence deals" for reference and the Ministry had declined to do 
so. The PAC had never requested for the CVC Report on procurement 
transaction relating to OP Vijay (Army). 
On careful consideration of the relevant document received from 
the Lok Sabha Secretariat, the factual position emerges as follows: 
'The genesis of CVC's Report on def ence deals lies in the decision 
taken by the Minister of Defence to request CVC (vide letter of 
14.2.2000) to investigate/study th e defence deals since 1989 in the 
background of certain allegations made during Short Duration 
Discussion in Rajya Sabha on 23rd December 1999, and also in a writ 
petition filed in Delhi High Court by Rear Admiral S.V. Purohit. The 
terms of reference of investigati on into the defence deals since 1989 
were as follows:- 
- All major contracts entered into by the MoD and the Services 
Headquarters for defence procurements since the ban on 
involvement of agents was imposed by the Government.

- Allegations of irregularities and corruption made in the writ 
petition of Rear Admiral S.V. Purohit. 
- Cases-of contracts worth Rs. 75 crore and more in value.

"The Public Account Committee of Parliament are examining the.

dated 23.O8.2001 responded that an "Interim Report on the subject 
of defence deals was submitted to the Government on 7th August,

secret." CVC also advised that "the files concerned with the 
Reports are with the Ministry of Defence", and as such "PAC may

CVC, vide their letter dated 23.8.2001, had also conveyed to

deals' entrusted as per terms of reference conveyed to CVC 
by MoD.

PAC at its sitting held on 19th December, 2001 decided to 
take up for detailed examination the entire Report of C&AG on 
"Review of Procurement for OP Vijay (Army)", which had been 
tabled in Parliament on 11th December, 2001. 
In the above context, PAC asked the Ministry of Defence to

position to supply a copy of the CVC Report on defence deals

Members have also pointed out that th e prescribed procedure and practice 
for drafting of the Minutes and the Report of the Committee were not 
observed. 
On the basis of the above facts, available documents and relevant 
papers, I find that CVC was neither assigned nor has conducted any 
investigations or given any Report as such on the subject of 'procurement 
for OP Vijay (Army)'. CVC had confirmed this to the PAC Secretariat. 
"However, as a measure of abundant c aution, I asked the Secretary-General 
to recheck with CVC. CVC has reconf irmed in writing that, "CVC has not 
conducted any investigations into pr ocurements for OP Vijay (Army) i.e. 
related to the Kargil Operations". 
In regard to investigation into defence deals conducted by CVC on 
the request of MoD, out of all the items taken up for investigation, only 2
